lines.vo: Why do you keep leaving everything for future you?
That's not bad time management. Your brain treats future you like someone else.
Kev plans his tasks in his Daily Habit Builder, then pushes them all to tomorrow.
In brain scan studies, thinking about your future self looked a lot like thinking about a stranger.
So dumping work on future you feels like dumping it on somebody else.
And people who felt closer to their future selves tended to make more patient choices.
So shrink the task to five minutes, and do it as today you.
One small box, checked today. That's how you stay on track.
